edits.new: For each question, split a compound parent phrase into independently required conditions and quote only one condition. Before testing a shared kind or action, choose a further qualification imposed by the parent that the child's own wording does not explicitly impose. Prioritize identity or consumer if several such qualifications remain. Ask which admitted child case falls outside that qualification, even if you expect a necessary implication to exclude it. Test that exclusion in the answer rather than replacing the question with a shared condition. Preserve the child's kind or activity and all its other requirements; a shared name does not import the parent's additional qualifications. Identify the child's wording or ordinary-language implication that a variation contradicts. If that lexical boundary cannot be settled, leave admission unresolved. Apply each condition to what it constrains and test exclusion across every parent alternative and permitted topic connection. Neither missing explicit wording nor a failed candidate establishes the coverage answer.
edits.old: For each question, split a compound parent phrase into independently required conditions and quote only one condition. If the parent expressly restricts identity or consumer and the child's own meaning does not explicitly impose that restriction, choose it before any shared action, property or purpose condition. Ask which admitted child case concerns someone or something outside that restriction, even if you expect a necessary implication to exclude it. Test that exclusion in the answer rather than replacing the question with a different condition. Apply the restriction to what it constrains and retain every permitted topic connection. A failed candidate does not establish complete coverage; the absence of matching explicit wording does not establish a counterexample.
